name: Standard Push-Up
description: Bodyweight pressing movement performed in a plank position.
key_principles: Core-to-upper body integration.
key_technical_checkpoints: Hands slightly wider than shoulders; body moves as one rigid unit; elbows stay tucked.
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than your shoulders on the floor. Your legs should be extended behind you, and your body should form a straight line from your head to your heels.
Engage your core by tightening your abdominal muscles to prevent your hips from sagging.
Inhale as you lower your body toward the floor by bending your elbows. Keep your elbows tucked in at a 45-degree angle to your body to protect your shoulders.
Lower yourself until your chest is just above the floor or as far as you can go with good form.
Exhale as you push through your hands, extending your arms to return to the starting plank position. Focus on using your chest muscles to drive the movement.
Keep your neck in a neutral position by looking at the floor slightly ahead of you throughout the exercise.

name: Goblet Squat
description: Squatting while holding a weight against the chest.
key_principles: Mastering squat mechanics with a front-loaded weight.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep weight tight to chest; use elbows to push knees out; maintain a flat back.
instructions: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with your toes pointed slightly outward. Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against your chest with both hands, cupping the top of the weight. Keep your elbows tucked in.
Brace your core to keep your back straight and your chest up. This will help you maintain an upright posture throughout the movement.
Inhale and begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees. Descend until your hips are lower than your knees, keeping your heels flat on the floor.
Keep your chest proud and your elbows inside your knees at the bottom of the squat.
Exhale and drive through your heels to return to the starting position, squeezing your glutes at the top to complete the repetition.
Maintain a controlled tempo, focusing on the quality of each repetition rather than speed.

name: Plank
description: Holding a push-up position on the forearms.
key_principles: Isometric core stability and anti-extension.
key_technical_checkpoints: Flat back; squeeze glutes; shoulders directly over elbows.
instructions: Begin in a prone position on the floor. Place your forearms on the ground with your elbows aligned directly under your shoulders and your hands clasped or flat on the floor.
Extend your legs straight behind you, with your feet together or hip-width apart. Your weight should be supported by your forearms and the balls of your feet.
Engage your core by drawing your navel in towards your spine and squeezing your glutes. This will create a stable, straight line from your head to your heels.
Ensure your back is flat and not arched or rounded. Your hips should be in line with your shoulders, not sagging or piked up.
Keep your head in a neutral position with your gaze directed towards the floor in front of you.
Hold this static position for the intended duration, breathing deeply and consistently.

name: Lat Pulldown
description: Sitting and pulling a weighted bar down toward the upper chest.
key_principles: Vertical pulling with controlled resistance.
key_technical_checkpoints: Avoid leaning back excessively; pull with elbows, not hands.
instructions: Sit down at the lat pulldown machine and adjust the knee pad so that it fits snugly against your thighs, preventing your body from lifting during the exercise.
Grasp the bar with a wide, overhand grip (pronated grip), with your hands positioned wider than your shoulders.
With your arms fully extended, lean back slightly (about 20-30 degrees) and create a slight arch in your lower back. Keep your chest up and your core engaged.
Exhale and pull the bar down towards your upper chest by drawing your shoulder blades down and back. Focus on using your back muscles to initiate the pull.
Continue pulling until the bar is just below your chin or touches your upper chest. Squeeze your lats at the peak of the contraction.
Inhale and slowly return the bar to the starting position with your arms fully extended, maintaining control throughout the eccentric phase.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: Lifting dumbbells out to the sides.
key_principles: Lateral deltoid isolation.
key_technical_checkpoints: Lean slightly forward; lead with elbows; don't lift above shoulder height.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides. Your palms should be facing your body.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows and keep your chest up, shoulders back, and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Exhale and lift the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc until they are at shoulder level. Keep your arms almost straight, but with a slight bend in the elbows.
Focus on leading the movement with your elbows to ensure you are using your deltoids rather than your traps.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder muscles.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, resisting the pull of gravity.

name: Barbell Bench Press
description: Lying on a bench, pressing a barbell from chest to full arm extension.
key_principles: Horizontal pushing power and structural stability.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep elbows tucked at 45 degrees; maintain 5 points of contact; bar path is slightly diagonal.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet planted firmly on the ground. Your back should have a slight, natural arch, and your shoulder blades should be retracted and pressed into the bench.
Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Your pinkies or ring fingers should be on the knurl rings of the barbell.
Unrack the bar and position it directly over your shoulders with your arms fully extended.
Inhale and lower the bar in a controlled manner to your mid-chest (around the sternum). Your elbows should be tucked at about a 45-degree angle to your body.
Lightly touch the bar to your chest, pausing for a second if necessary to control the weight.

Exhale and press the bar back up to the starting position by driving your feet into the floor and extending your arms. The bar path should be a slight arc, moving from your chest back over your shoulders.

name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
description: Hinge movement lowering weights while keeping legs mostly straight.
key_principles: Hamstring and glute isolation via the hip hinge.
key_technical_checkpoints: Move hips backward; go only until you feel a deep stretch in hamstrings.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell or dumbbells with an overhand grip in front of your thighs. Your knees should have a slight bend.
Keeping your back straight, initiate the movement by hinging at your hips and pushing your glutes backward. Maintain a proud chest and engaged core.
Lower the weight by sliding it down your thighs, keeping the bar as close to your body as possible. Your shins should remain vertical.
Descend until you feel a significant stretch in your hamstrings, typically when the weight is at mid-shin level. Do not round your lower back.
Reverse the movement by driving your hips forward and squeezing your glutes to return to a standing position.
Finish the movement by standing tall. Avoid hyperextending your back at the top.

name: Barbell Back Squat
description: Squatting with a bar on the upper back.
key_principles: Lower body strength and axial loading management.
key_technical_checkpoints: Sit back into hips; knees track over toes; keep chest up.
instructions: Set up the barbell in a squat rack at the height of your upper chest. Position yourself under the bar, allowing it to rest on your upper traps, not on your neck.
Grasp the bar with a firm, overhand grip, slightly wider than your shoulders. Keep your wrists straight and your elbows pointing down.
Lift the bar from the rack by extending your legs. Take one or two steps back to clear the rack, and position your feet shoulder-width apart with your toes pointing slightly outward.
Brace your core, keep your chest up, and maintain a neutral spine. Inhale and begin the descent by pushing your hips back and bending your knees simultaneously.
Squat down until your hip crease is below your knees (below parallel). Ensure your knees track in line with your feet and do not collapse inward.
Exhale and drive through your mid-foot to ascend, maintaining an upright torso. Extend your hips and knees to return to the starting position.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: Hanging from a bar and lifting legs toward the chest.
key_principles: Advanced abdominal strength and grip endurance.
key_technical_checkpoints: Don't swing; focus on curling the pelvis upward toward the ribs.
instructions: Grasp a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, with your hands positioned shoulder-width apart. Let your body hang with your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and keep your legs straight with your feet together. Try to minimize any swinging or use of momentum.
Exhale and raise your legs in a controlled manner until they are parallel to the floor, forming a 90-degree angle with your torso.
Focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift your legs. For an increased challenge, aim to bring your toes all the way up to the bar.
Inhale as you slowly lower your legs back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the eccentric phase.
To modify the exercise, you can perform bent-knee raises by tucking your knees towards your chest.

name: Traditional Deadlift
description: Lifting a loaded barbell from the ground to hip height.
key_principles: Maximum posterior chain strength and total body bracing.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep back flat; drive with legs; bar stays close to body.
instructions: Approach the barbell so that it is centered over your feet. Your feet should be about hip-width apart, with the bar dissecting the middle of your feet.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to grip the bar. Your hands should be placed just outside of your shins. Use a double overhand or mixed grip.
Lower your hips and flatten your back. Your chest should be up, your shoulders should be slightly in front of the bar, and your shins should be in contact with the bar.
Take a deep breath, brace your core, and initiate the lift by driving your feet through the floor. Keep the bar close to your body as you extend your knees and hips.
As the bar passes your knees, drive your hips forward to meet the bar and achieve a fully upright position. Squeeze your glutes at the top of the lift.
To lower the bar, reverse the motion by hinging at your hips first, and then bending your knees once the bar has cleared them. Maintain control of the bar until it is back on the floor.

name: Chest Dips
description: Lowering and lifting the body using parallel bars.
key_principles: Vertical pressing targeting the lower pectorals.
key_technical_checkpoints: Lean forward for chest focus; keep shoulders stable.
instructions: Position yourself between a set of parallel bars and grip them with your hands. Extend your arms to lift your body above the bars.
To target the chest, lean your torso forward at a 30 to 45-degree angle. To emphasize the triceps, keep your torso as upright as possible.
Inhale and slowly lower your body by bending your elbows. Continue descending until you feel a good stretch in your chest or your shoulders are slightly below your elbows.
Keep your elbows tucked in close to your body to protect your shoulder joints.
Exhale and press through your palms to drive your body back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
At the top of the movement, squeeze your chest and triceps before beginning the next repetition.

name: Pull-Up
description: Lifting bodyweight to a bar using an overhand grip.
key_principles: Vertical pulling and relative strength.
key_technical_checkpoints: Dead hang start; pull chest to bar; control the descent.
instructions: Grasp a pull-up bar with an overhand (pronated) grip, with your hands positioned slightly wider than your shoulders.
Begin from a dead hang, with your arms fully extended and your body in a straight line. Engage your core to prevent swinging.
Initiate the pull by retracting your scapulae (pulling your shoulder blades down and back).
Exhale and pull yourself up by driving your elbows down towards the floor. Focus on using your back muscles to lift your body.
Continue pulling until your chin clears the bar. Keep your chest up and your gaze forward.
Inhale and lower your body back to the starting position in a controlled manner, fully extending your arms at the bottom.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: Single-leg squat with rear foot elevated.
key_principles: Unilateral strength and balance.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep front heel planted; maintain upright or slightly leaned torso.
instructions: Stand a few feet in front of a bench or elevated platform. Place the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Your front foot should be positioned far enough forward so that when you lower into the squat, your front knee forms a 90-degree angle and does not travel past your toes.
Hold dumbbells in each hand with a neutral grip (optional). Keep your torso upright, your chest up, and your core engaged.
Inhale and lower your body in a controlled manner until your front thigh is parallel to the ground. Your back knee should hover just above the floor.
Exhale and drive through your front heel to return to the starting position, maintaining your balance and posture.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching to the other leg.

name: Arnold Press
description: Shoulder press with a rotational wrist movement.
key_principles: Multi-planar deltoid engagement.
key_technical_checkpoints: Rotate palms toward you at bottom, away at top.
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Start with the dumbbells at shoulder height, with your palms facing your body and your elbows bent.
Keep your core engaged and your back pressed firmly against the bench.
Exhale and begin to press the dumbbells overhead. As you press upward, rotate your wrists so that your palms face forward at the top of the movement.
Continue pressing until your arms are fully extended but not locked out. Your biceps should be next to your ears.
Inhale and reverse the movement, rotating your wrists so that your palms are facing your body again as you lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Maintain a smooth and controlled motion throughout the entire exercise.

name: Skull Crushers
description: Lowering a bar toward the forehead while lying down.
key_principles: Tricep long-head activation through stretch.
key_technical_checkpoints: Upper arms stationary; lower slightly behind the head.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly on the floor. Hold an EZ bar or two dumbbells with an overhand, narrow grip (about shoulder-width apart) and extend your arms directly above your chest.
Keeping your upper arms stationary and perpendicular to the floor, inhale and slowly lower the weight by bending your elbows.
Lower the bar towards your forehead until your elbows are at a 90-degree angle. Your forearms should be just above parallel to the floor.
Keep your elbows tucked in and avoid letting them flare out to the sides.
Exhale and press the weight back to the starting position by extending your elbows and flexing your triceps.
Focus on a controlled movement, particularly during the eccentric (lowering) phase, to maximize triceps engagement.

name: Kettlebell Swing
description: Swinging a kettlebell through a hip hinge motion.
key_principles: Explosive posterior chain power.
key_technical_checkpoints: Hinge at hips, don't squat; snap hips forward to move weight.
instructions: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with a kettlebell placed about a foot in front of you on the floor.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to grip the kettlebell with both hands using an overhand grip. Keep your back flat and your chest up.
Initiate the swing by 'hiking' the kettlebell back between your legs, as if you were snapping a football.
In one explosive movement, drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to propel the kettlebell upward. Your arms should act as a pendulum, guiding the weight, not lifting it.
The kettlebell should swing to about chest height. At the top of the swing, your body should form a straight line from your head to your heels.
Allow the kettlebell to swing back down between your legs as you hinge at your hips, preparing for the next repetition. Maintain control of the weight throughout the movement.

name: Box Jumps
description: Jumping onto an elevated platform.
key_principles: Plyometric explosive power and landing mechanics.
key_technical_checkpoints: Land softly; step down to protect joints.
instructions: Select a sturdy box of an appropriate height. Stand facing the box with your feet positioned shoulder-width apart.
Initiate the movement by performing a shallow squat, swinging your arms back to load up for the jump.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles (triple extension) while swinging your arms forward to generate maximum upward momentum.
As you jump, tuck your knees towards your chest and aim to land softly on the center of the box with both feet simultaneously.
Upon landing, absorb the impact by bending your knees and hips into a partial squat position. Ensure your entire foot is on the box.
Stand up tall on the box to complete the repetition, then step down carefully one foot at a time. Do not jump down.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
description: Pressing dumbbells on a 30-45 degree incline.
key_principles: Upper chest (clavicular head) targeting.
key_technical_checkpoints: Shoulders back and down; control dumbbells on the descent.
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 30-45 degree incline. Sit on the edge of the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
To get into position, 'kick' the dumbbells up to your shoulders one at a time as you lie back on the bench. Plant your feet firmly on the floor.
Your head and back should be firmly pressed against the bench. Press the dumbbells up over your chest with your palms facing forward and your arms fully extended.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells to the sides of your upper chest in a controlled arc. Your elbows should be tucked at a 45 to 60-degree angle relative to your torso.
Lower the weights until you feel a good stretch in your chest, with the dumbbells roughly level with your shoulders.
Exhale and press the dumbbells back up to the starting position, squeezing your pectoral muscles at the top of the movement.

name: Seated Cable Row
description: Pulling a cable handle toward the waist while seated.
key_principles: Mid-back development and posture.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep chest up; squeeze shoulder blades at the peak.
instructions: Sit at a cable row machine and place your feet securely on the foot platform. Your knees should be slightly bent.
Grasp the V-bar or straight bar attachment with a neutral or overhand grip. Sit upright with a straight back, chest out, and shoulders pulled back and down.
With your arms fully extended, pull the handle towards your lower abdomen by retracting your shoulder blades and driving your elbows back.
Keep your torso stationary throughout the movement, avoiding the use of momentum by leaning back and forth.
Squeeze your back muscles at the peak of the contraction, holding for a brief moment.
Inhale and slowly extend your arms to return the handle to the starting position, maintaining control and feeling a stretch in your lats.

name: Leg Press
description: Pushing a weighted platform with the feet.
key_principles: Quad isolation with low spinal stress.
key_technical_checkpoints: Don't lock knees; keep lower back flat on the pad.
instructions: Sit down on the leg press machine and place your feet on the platform, positioned about shoulder-width apart with your toes pointing slightly outward.
Ensure your back and head are resting comfortably against the padded support. Your hips should be positioned securely at the bottom of the seat.
Press the platform to full extension to release the safety catches, but do not lock your knees.
Inhale and slowly lower the platform by bending your knees until they form a 90-degree angle or until your thighs are close to your chest.
Keep your feet flat on the platform and do not allow your lower back to round or lift off the seat pad.
Exhale and press the platform back to the starting position by driving through your heels and mid-foot, extending your legs. Avoid locking out your knees at the top of the movement.

name: Overhead Press
description: Standing barbell press to full overhead lockout.
key_principles: Vertical pressing and full body tension.
key_technical_checkpoints: Squeeze glutes; bar path stays close to face; head through at top.
instructions: Set up a barbell in a squat rack at shoulder height. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than your shoulders, with your palms facing forward.
Position the bar in the front rack position, resting on your anterior deltoids and clavicles. Your elbows should be pointing slightly forward.
Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and take a deep breath. Press the bar directly overhead by extending your arms fully.
As the bar passes your head, push your head 'through the window' so that the bar is aligned over your spine at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back to the starting front rack position in a controlled manner.
Avoid using your legs to generate momentum (this would be a push press). The movement should be a strict press using only your upper body strength.

name: Barbell Bicep Curl
description: Curling a barbell using a supinated grip.
key_principles: Bicep hypertrophy through isolation.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep elbows pinned; avoid using body momentum.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a supinated (underhand) grip. Your hands should be positioned about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and your chest up. Your arms should be fully extended at the start.
Exhale and curl the barbell upward by contracting your biceps. Focus on keeping your upper arms stationary; only your forearms should move.
Continue curling until the bar is at shoulder level and your biceps are fully contracted. Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the weight. The movement should be strict and isolated to the biceps.

name: Bicycle Crunches
description: Supine core rotation with pedaling legs.
key_principles: Engaging obliques and rectus abdominis.
key_technical_checkpoints: Opposite elbow to knee; move slowly and with control.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your hands behind your head, lightly supporting it. Your knees should be bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Lift your shoulders off the floor and bring your knees up to a 90-degree angle, with your shins parallel to the floor.
Engage your core and begin a 'pedaling' motion with your legs, extending one leg out while bringing the opposite knee towards your chest.
Simultaneously, twist your torso to bring your opposite elbow towards your incoming knee. For example, as you bring your right knee in, twist to meet it with your left elbow.
Alternate sides in a smooth, controlled motion, keeping your core engaged and your lower back pressed into the floor.
Focus on the rotation of your torso and the contraction of your obliques, rather than pulling on your neck with your hands.

name: Burpees
description: Combination of squat, plank, push-up, and jump.
key_principles: Metabolic conditioning and full body power.
key_technical_checkpoints: Maintain core tension; land flat-footed on the jump.
instructions: Start in a standing position with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body into a squat position and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Kick your feet back into a plank position, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Perform a push-up by lowering your chest to the floor and pushing back up.
Jump your feet back towards your hands, returning to a squat position.
Explode into a jump, reaching your arms overhead. Land softly and immediately begin the next repetition.

name: Cable Crossover
description: Bringing cable handles together across the midline.
key_principles: Constant tension throughout the pectorals.
key_technical_checkpoints: Chest out; slight elbow bend; hard squeeze at center.
instructions: Set the pulleys on a cable machine to a high position, above your head. Attach D-handles to each pulley.
Grasp a handle in each hand and step forward into a staggered stance to create tension on the cables.
Lean slightly forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your chest up. Your arms should be extended out to your sides with a slight bend in your elbows.
Exhale and bring the handles together in a wide arc in front of your body. Focus on squeezing your chest muscles to initiate the movement.
Continue until your hands meet at the midline of your body. Squeeze your chest for a moment at the peak contraction.
Inhale and slowly reverse the movement, returning your arms to the starting position in a controlled manner.

name: Face Pulls
description: Pulling a cable rope toward the forehead.
key_principles: Shoulder health and rear deltoid isolation.
key_technical_checkpoints: Pull rope apart; thumbs pointing back; keep elbows high.
instructions: Set a pulley on a cable machine to head height or slightly above. Attach a rope handle.
Grasp the rope with an overhand grip, with your thumbs pointing towards you. Step back to create tension on the cable.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and maintain a slight bend in your knees. Keep your chest up and your core engaged.
Exhale and pull the rope towards your face by retracting your shoulder blades and externally rotating your shoulders. Your hands should go towards your ears.
Focus on leading with your elbows and keeping them high, above your shoulders. Squeeze your rear deltoids and upper back muscles at the peak of the contraction.
Inhale and slowly return the rope to the starting position in a controlled manner, resisting the pull of the cable.

name: Hip Thrust
description: Weighted bridge with shoulders on a bench.
key_principles: Maximal glute activation and hip extension.
key_technical_checkpoints: Vertical shins at top; chin tucked; full hip lockout.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench. Place a barbell across your hips. Your knees should be bent and your feet flat on the floor, about shoulder-width apart.
Your shoulder blades should be positioned on the edge of the bench. You can use a pad on the barbell for comfort.
Keeping your chin tucked, drive through your heels to lift your hips towards the ceiling. Your body should form a straight line from your shoulders to your knees at the top of the movement.
Your shins should be vertical at the top of the thrust. Squeeze your glutes powerfully at the peak contraction.
Lower your hips back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Avoid arching your lower back; the movement should be driven by your glutes.

name: Tricep Pushdown
description: Pushing a cable bar/rope down by extending elbows.
key_principles: Tricep isolation and elbow health.
key_technical_checkpoints: Upper arms stationary; full extension at bottom.
instructions: Attach a straight bar or rope to a high pulley on a cable machine. Grasp the attachment with an overhand grip, with your hands positioned about shoulder-width apart.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in your knees. Lean slightly forward at the hips.
Start with your elbows bent and tucked into your sides. Your forearms should be parallel to the floor or slightly above.
Exhale and press the bar down by extending your elbows. Keep your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
Continue pressing until your arms are fully extended. Squeeze your triceps at the bottom of the movement.
Inhale and slowly return the bar to the starting position in a controlled manner.

name: Dead Bug
description: Lowering opposite arm and leg while lying on back.
key_principles: Spinal stability and core control.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep lower back glued to the floor; move slowly.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Raise your arms towards the ceiling.
Lift your feet off the floor and bring your knees up to a 90-degree angle, so your shins are parallel to the floor. This is the starting position.
Engage your core, pressing your lower back into the floor. There should be no arch in your back.
Slowly lower your right arm and left leg towards the floor simultaneously, keeping your core tight.
Lower them as far as you can without your lower back arching off the floor. Then, return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side, lowering your left arm and right leg. Continue alternating sides in a slow, controlled manner.

name: Mountain Climbers
description: Alternating knee drives in a plank position.
key_principles: Cardiovascular endurance and core stability.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep hips low; shoulders over hands.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from your head to your heels.
Engage your core to keep your back flat and your hips stable.
Drive your right knee towards your chest, then quickly switch and drive your left knee towards your chest.
Continue alternating knees in a running motion, keeping your core tight and your upper body stable.
Maintain a quick, consistent pace, as if you are running in place in a plank position.
Avoid letting your hips bounce up and down; the movement should be controlled and driven by your core and legs.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
description: Pulling a bar to the waist while hinged.
key_principles: Horizontal pulling for back thickness.
key_technical_checkpoints: Neutral spine; pull elbows past the ribs; control the bar.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip. Your knees should be slightly bent.
Hinge at your hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Let the barbell hang directly in front of you with your arms fully extended.
Exhale and pull the barbell up towards your lower chest by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Keep your elbows tucked in and pull them past your torso. Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.

name: Walking Lunges
description: Stepping forward into alternating lunges.
key_principles: Dynamic balance and lower body isolation.
key_technical_checkpoints: Upright torso; front knee over ankle; 90-degree angles.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet together. You can hold dumbbells in each hand for added resistance.
Take a step forward with your right leg, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Your front knee should be directly above your ankle, and your back knee should be hovering just above the ground.
Keep your torso upright and your core engaged.
Push off your back foot and bring it forward to meet your front foot, returning to a standing position.
Repeat the movement, this time stepping forward with your left leg. Continue alternating legs as you 'walk' forward.

name: Hammer Curl
description: Neutral grip bicep curl.
key_principles: Targeting the brachialis and brachioradialis.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep palms facing each other; no wrist rotation.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral (hammer) grip, so your palms are facing each other.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and your chest up. Your arms should be fully extended at the start.
Exhale and curl the dumbbells upward by contracting your biceps and brachialis muscles. Keep your palms facing each other throughout the movement.
Continue curling until the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the weight. The movement should be strict and isolated.

name: Russian Twist
description: Seated torso rotation.
key_principles: Oblique strength and coordination.
key_technical_checkpoints: Follow hands with gaze; keep feet elevated for challenge.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat on the ground. Lean back slightly, so your torso is at a 45-degree angle to the floor. Keep your back straight.
For a greater challenge, lift your feet off the ground. You can hold a weight or medicine ball with both hands for added resistance.
Engage your core and twist your torso to the right, bringing the weight or your hands towards the right side of your body.
Then, twist to the left, bringing the weight or your hands to the left side of your body. This completes one repetition.
Continue alternating sides in a controlled motion, keeping your core tight and your back straight.
Avoid rounding your back or using momentum to swing the weight. The rotation should come from your obliques.

name: Skater Hops
description: Lateral explosive jumps.
key_principles: Lateral power and athletic stability.
key_technical_checkpoints: Land softly; stick the landing; use arms for balance.
instructions: Start in a standing position with your feet together.
Hop to your right, landing on your right foot with your right knee bent. Your left leg should swing behind your right leg.
As you land, swing your arms to the right to help with balance and momentum.
Then, hop to your left, landing on your left foot with your left knee bent. Your right leg should swing behind your left leg.
Continue hopping from side to side in a continuous, fluid motion, like a speed skater.
Focus on covering distance laterally and maintaining your balance with each hop.

name: Inverted Row
description: Horizontal row under a bar with feet on the ground.
key_principles: Bodyweight pulling for back strength.
key_technical_checkpoints: Body in straight line; pull chest to bar.
instructions: Set a barbell in a squat rack at about waist height. The higher the bar, the easier the exercise will be.
Position yourself under the bar, lying on your back. Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Extend your legs out in front of you, with your heels on the ground. Your body should form a straight line from your head to your heels.
Engage your core and glutes to keep your body rigid. Exhale and pull your chest up towards the bar by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Pause at the top of the movement when your chest is close to or touching the bar.
Inhale and slowly lower your body back to the starting position in a controlled manner.

name: Leg Extension
description: Seated leg extension against resistance.
key_principles: Pure quad isolation.
key_technical_checkpoints: Align knee with machine pivot; control descent.
instructions: Sit on a leg extension machine and adjust the back pad so your knees are at the edge of the seat. Your knees should be aligned with the machine's pivot point.
Position the lower leg pad so it rests on your shins, just above your ankles.
Grasp the handles on the side of the machine for stability.
Exhale and extend your legs to lift the weight until your legs are straight. Do not lock your knees at the top.
Squeeze your quadriceps at the top of the movement for a moment.
Inhale and slowly lower the weight back to the starting position in a controlled manner.

name: Rear Delt Fly
description: Hinged lateral lift for the back of the shoulder.
key_principles: Rear deltoid isolation and upper back health.
key_technical_checkpoints: Pinkies up; squeeze shoulder blades; keep spine flat.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench or stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge at your hips so your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Let the dumbbells hang directly below your chest with your palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Exhale and raise the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, leading with your elbows.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement. Your arms should be parallel to the floor.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.

name: Preacher Curl
description: Curling on a slanted support pad.
key_principles: Strict bicep isolation without momentum.
key_technical_checkpoints: Full extension at bottom; armpits tight to pad.
instructions: Adjust the seat of a preacher curl bench so that your armpits are resting near the top of the pad.
Grasp an EZ bar or dumbbells with an underhand grip, and sit down with your upper arms resting on the pad.
Your arms should be fully extended at the start of the movement.
Exhale and curl the weight upward by contracting your biceps. Keep your upper arms and body stationary.
Continue curling until the weight is at shoulder level and your biceps are fully contracted. Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Inhale and slowly lower the weight back to the starting position in a controlled manner, feeling a stretch in your biceps.

name: Bird Dog
description: Extending opposite arm and leg on all fours.
key_principles: Spinal stability and balance.
key_technical_checkpoints: Don't arch back; reach long; keep hips square.
instructions: Start on all fours, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips. Your back should be flat.
Engage your core to keep your spine in a neutral position.
Simultaneously extend your right arm straight out in front of you and your left leg straight out behind you.
Keep your hips and shoulders square to the floor. Avoid arching your back or rotating your hips.
Hold for a moment, then return to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat on the other side, extending your left arm and right leg. Continue alternating sides.

name: High Knees
description: Running in place with high knee drives.
key_principles: Cardiovascular speed and hip flexor engagement.
key_technical_checkpoints: Stay on balls of feet; drive knees to hip height.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Begin by jogging in place, driving your right knee up towards your chest as high as you can.
As you lower your right leg, drive your left knee up towards your chest.
Continue alternating knees in a running motion, maintaining a quick pace.
Use your arms to help with momentum, swinging them in opposition to your legs.
Stay on the balls of your feet and keep your core engaged throughout the exercise.

name: Machine Chest Press
description: Seated horizontal press using a machine.
key_principles: Foundational chest strength with guided path.
key_technical_checkpoints: Set seat height at mid-chest; keep back against pad.
instructions: Adjust the seat of the machine so the handles are at mid-chest level. Sit with your back firmly against the pad.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, and plant your feet firmly on the floor.
Exhale and press the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, but not locked out.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Inhale and slowly return the handles to the starting position in a controlled manner, feeling a stretch in your chest.
Avoid letting the weight stack touch down between repetitions to maintain tension on the muscles.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
description: Sawing motion dumbbell pull.
key_principles: Unilateral back strength and core stability.
key_technical_checkpoints: Pull toward hip; keep back flat; avoid torso twist.
instructions: Place your left knee and left hand on a flat bench, with your right foot planted firmly on the floor.
Your torso should be parallel to the floor, and your back should be straight. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with a neutral grip.
Let the dumbbell hang directly below your shoulder with your arm fully extended.
Exhale and pull the dumbbell up towards your hip by retracting your shoulder blade and bending your elbow.
Keep your elbow close to your body and squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner. Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other.

name: Standing Calf Raise
description: Rising on toes with weight.
key_principles: Calf muscle hypertrophy.
key_technical_checkpoints: Full stretch at bottom; hard squeeze at top.
instructions: Stand with your feet flat on the floor or with the balls of your feet on an elevated surface, like a step or calf raise block.
You can perform this exercise with bodyweight, holding dumbbells, or using a calf raise machine.
If using weights, hold them at your sides or rest a barbell on your upper back.
Exhale and press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as you can. Squeeze your calf muscles at the top of the movement.
Hold the peak contraction for a moment.
Inhale and slowly lower your heels back to the starting position, feeling a stretch in your calves if you are using an elevated surface.

name: Upright Row
description: Pulling weight vertically toward chin.
key_principles: Side delt and trap activation.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep bar close; elbows above wrists; pull to mid-chest.
instructions: Grasp a barbell or EZ bar with an overhand grip, with your hands positioned slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.
Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms fully extended, with the bar resting against your thighs.
Exhale and pull the bar straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows. Keep the bar close to your body.
Your elbows should be higher than your wrists at the top of the movement. Pull the bar up to your lower chest or upper abdomen.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your traps and deltoids.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position in a controlled manner.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
description: Bench press with narrow hand placement.
key_principles: Tricep-dominant pressing strength.
key_technical_checkpoints: Hands shoulder-width; elbows close to body.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands positioned shoulder-width apart or slightly narrower.
Unrack the bar and hold it directly over your chest with your arms fully extended.
Inhale and lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked in close to your body.
Lightly touch the bar to your chest.
Exhale and press the bar back up to the starting position by extending your arms, focusing on using your triceps to drive the movement.
Avoid flaring your elbows out to the sides; keep them tucked to maximize tricep engagement.

name: Side Plank
description: Balancing on one forearm sideways.
key_principles: Oblique and lateral core stability.
key_technical_checkpoints: Keep hips high; straight body alignment.
instructions: Lie on your right side with your legs straight and stacked on top of each other.
Place your right elbow directly under your shoulder, with your forearm perpendicular to your body.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from your head to your feet.
Your weight should be supported by your right forearm and the side of your right foot.
Hold this position for the desired amount of time, then repeat on the other side.
Avoid letting your hips sag towards the floor; keep them lifted and your core engaged.

name: Bear Crawl
description: Moving on all fours with hovering knees.
key_principles: Dynamic core and coordination.
key_technical_checkpoints: Flat back; small movements; knees close to floor.
instructions: Start on all fours, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips.
Lift your knees off the floor so they are hovering just above the ground. Your back should be flat.
Move forward by taking a small step with your right hand and left foot simultaneously.
Then, take a small step with your left hand and right foot simultaneously.
Continue crawling forward in this contralateral pattern, keeping your back flat and your knees close to the floor.
You can also crawl backward or laterally for an added challenge.

name: Jumping Jacks
description: Classic jumping arm/leg spread.
key_principles: Metabolic warm-up and coordination.
key_technical_checkpoints: Soft landing; full arm range.
instructions: Stand with your feet together and your arms at your sides.
In one fluid motion, jump your feet out to the sides, wider than your shoulders, while simultaneously raising your arms out to the sides and overhead.
Your arms should meet above your head.
Then, jump back to the starting position, bringing your feet together and your arms back to your sides.
Continue this movement for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
Maintain a steady rhythm and land softly on the balls of your feet.

name: Decline Bench Press
description: Barbell press on a decline bench targeting lower chest fibers with greater range of motion.
key_principles: Lower chest emphasis, control the descent, drive through chest not shoulders, maintain shoulder blade retraction.
key_technical_checkpoints: Bar touches lower chest, elbows 45-degree angle, feet secured, arch maintained, full lockout at top.
instructions: Secure feet at the end of decline bench, lie back with bar above lower chest
Grip bar slightly wider than shoulder-width, unrack with straight arms
Lower bar in controlled manner to lower chest, elbows at 45 degrees
Press bar up and slightly back toward face until arms fully extended
Pause briefly at top, squeeze chest, repeat for desired reps
Re-rack bar safely with spotter assistance if using heavy weight

name: Dumbbell Pullover
description: Classic exercise targeting chest and lats with emphasis on ribcage expansion and upper body stretch.
key_principles: Controlled arc motion, stretch at bottom, keep hips low, breathe deeply, focus on chest contraction.
key_technical_checkpoints: Elbows slightly bent, dumbbell path follows arc, deep stretch without shoulder pain, core engaged.
instructions: Lie perpendicular on bench with shoulders supported, hips below bench level
Hold one dumbbell with both hands above chest, slight bend in elbows
Lower dumbbell in arc behind head until stretch felt in chest and lats
Keep elbow angle constant throughout movement, breathe deeply at stretch
Pull dumbbell back to start position using chest and lats
Repeat maintaining constant tension and control throughout

name: Cable Chest Fly
description: Cable fly variation providing constant tension throughout the movement for chest isolation and definition.
key_principles: Constant tension, slight bend in elbows, focus on chest squeeze, control the eccentric, chest-level cables.
key_technical_checkpoints: Slight forward lean, elbows fixed angle, full stretch without shoulder impingement, squeeze at midline.
instructions: Set cables at chest height, grab handles, step forward into split stance
Lean slightly forward, arms extended with slight elbow bend
Bring handles together in front of chest in wide arc motion
Squeeze chest hard at peak contraction for 1-2 seconds
Control handles back to start position feeling deep chest stretch
Maintain same elbow angle throughout, repeat for desired reps

name: Diamond Push-Up
description: Close-grip push-up variation emphasizing inner chest and triceps with hands forming diamond shape.
key_principles: Hands close together, elbows tucked, controlled descent, full range of motion, core tight.
key_technical_checkpoints: Diamond hand position, body straight, chest touches hands, elbows stay close to body.
instructions: Start in plank position with hands close together forming diamond with index fingers and thumbs
Position hands directly under chest, body in straight line
Lower body by bending elbows, keeping them close to sides
Descend until chest nearly touches hands or until good stretch felt
Press back up powerfully until arms fully extended
Maintain rigid core throughout, repeat for desired reps

name: T-Bar Row
description: Compound rowing movement for building back thickness and strength using landmine or T-bar setup.
key_principles: Hinge at hips, chest up, pull to sternum, squeeze shoulder blades, neutral spine throughout.
key_technical_checkpoints: Flat back, knees bent, full range stretch, elbows drive back, controlled eccentric.
instructions: Straddle the bar with feet shoulder-width, hinge at hips with chest up
Grip handles or bar with neutral grip, arms fully extended
Pull bar toward lower chest by driving elbows back and up
Squeeze shoulder blades together at top of movement
Lower bar with control to full arm extension, maintaining back position
Repeat without letting plates touch floor between reps

name: Face Pull
description: Cable exercise targeting rear deltoids and upper back, crucial for shoulder health and posture.
key_principles: High cable position, pull to face, external rotation, squeeze rear delts, controlled tempo.
key_technical_checkpoints: Elbows high and wide, rope splits at face, shoulder blades retracted, no forward lean.
instructions: Set cable at upper chest height, attach rope handle
Grip rope with neutral grip, step back to create tension
Pull rope toward face, splitting rope handles at face level
Keep elbows high and wide, externally rotate shoulders
Squeeze shoulder blades and rear delts at peak contraction
Slowly return to start position with control, repeat

name: Wide Grip Pull-Up
description: Pull-up variation with wide grip emphasizing lat width and upper back development.
key_principles: Wide grip, pull to upper chest, full hang, shoulder blades lead, no swinging.
key_technical_checkpoints: Grip wider than shoulders, chest to bar, dead hang between reps, controlled descent.
instructions: Hang from bar with grip 6-8 inches wider than shoulder-width, palms forward
Start from full dead hang with arms completely straight
Initiate pull by depressing shoulder blades and engaging lats
Pull body up until upper chest touches or nears the bar
Lower with control back to full dead hang position
Avoid swinging or kipping, repeat for desired reps

name: Meadows Row
description: One-arm landmine row named after John Meadows, excellent for unilateral back development and core stability.
key_principles: Staggered stance, pull to hip, full stretch, rotation through torso, squeeze at top.
key_technical_checkpoints: Landmine setup, staggered stance, arm fully extends, pull through lat, no excessive trunk rotation.
instructions: Set up barbell in landmine, stand perpendicular with staggered stance
Bend at hips with chest up, grip end of bar with one hand
Pull bar toward hip in arcing motion, keeping elbow close
Rotate slightly through torso, squeeze lat at top position
Lower with control to full arm extension and stretch
Complete all reps on one side before switching

name: Chest-Supported Row
description: Row variation with chest support removing lower back stress, allowing focus on back muscles.
key_principles: Chest braced, pull with elbows, squeeze shoulder blades, no momentum, full range.
key_technical_checkpoints: Chest firmly against pad, neutral spine, elbows drive back, peak contraction hold.
instructions: Set incline bench to 45 degrees or use chest-supported row machine
Lie face down with chest firmly against pad, arms hanging straight
Grip dumbbells or handles with neutral or pronated grip
Pull weights toward lower chest by driving elbows back
Squeeze shoulder blades together at top, hold briefly
Lower with control to full extension, repeat

name: Front Squat
description: Barbell squat with bar positioned in front, heavily targeting quadriceps and requiring excellent mobility.
key_principles: Upright torso, elbows high, drive through full foot, core braced, controlled descent.
key_technical_checkpoints: Bar on front delts, elbows up, knees track toes, depth to parallel or below, vertical torso.
instructions: Approach bar, position on front deltoids with elbows high, clean grip or cross-arm grip
Unrack bar, step back, feet shoulder-width with slight toe out
Brace core hard, initiate squat by breaking at knees and hips simultaneously
Descend keeping elbows high and torso upright until thighs parallel or below
Drive through full foot, maintaining vertical torso angle
Stand to full extension, repeat while maintaining bar position and elbow height

name: Hack Squat
description: Machine-based squat variation isolating quadriceps with reduced spinal loading.
key_principles: Back against pad, controlled tempo, full range of motion, push through heels, knees aligned.
key_technical_checkpoints: Back flat on pad, feet mid-platform, knees track toes, depth controlled, no lockout bounce.
instructions: Position back against pad, shoulders under pads, feet mid-platform shoulder-width
Release safety handles, lower body by bending knees
Descend until thighs parallel to platform or deeper if mobility allows
Keep back pressed against pad, core engaged throughout
Drive through heels and mid-foot to press platform away
Extend to just before lockout, maintain tension, repeat

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
description: Intense bodyweight hamstring exercise focusing on eccentric strength, excellent for injury prevention.
key_principles: Controlled descent, use hamstrings to brake, push back up with hands if needed, gradual progression.
key_technical_checkpoints: Feet anchored, body straight, hamstrings engaged throughout, controlled eccentric phase.
instructions: Kneel on pad with feet secured under stable object or partner holding ankles
Keep body in straight line from knees to shoulders, arms ready to catch
Slowly lean forward, resisting with hamstrings as long as possible
Use hamstrings to control descent as body lowers toward ground
Catch yourself with hands at bottom, push back to start if needed
Over time, increase range and resistance as hamstring strength improves

name: Leg Curl
description: Isolation exercise for hamstrings using machine, lying or seated variation for posterior chain development.
key_principles: Full range of motion, squeeze at peak, slow eccentric, avoid using momentum, ankles flexed.
key_technical_checkpoints: Pad on lower calves, hips down, full extension to full flexion, no hip lift.
instructions: Lie face down on leg curl machine, pad positioned just above heels
Grip handles, keep hips pressed into pad throughout movement
Curl legs up by flexing knees, bringing heels toward glutes
Squeeze hamstrings hard at top position, hold briefly
Lower weight with control to full extension without letting weight stack touch
Maintain tension throughout, repeat for desired reps

name: Sissy Squat
description: Advanced bodyweight quad exercise with extreme knee flexion, building strength and resilience in quads and knees.
key_principles: Lean back while descending, knees push forward, maintain straight line, use support initially.
key_technical_checkpoints: Heels may lift, body leans back, knees well forward of toes, controlled range, gradual progression.
instructions: Stand with feet close together, hold support with one hand if needed
Rise onto balls of feet, maintain this position throughout
Lean entire body back while pushing knees forward
Lower body in controlled manner keeping torso and thighs in line
Descend until deep knee bend achieved, quads fully stretched
Contract quads to return to start position, repeat with control

name: Sumo Deadlift
description: Deadlift variation with wide stance emphasizing glutes, adductors and reducing range of motion.
key_principles: Wide stance, toes out, vertical shins, chest up, drive through floor, hip hinge pattern.
key_technical_checkpoints: Feet wide and angled out, knees track toes, arms inside legs, bar close to body, hips and shoulders rise together.
instructions: Approach bar with wide stance (feet near plates), toes angled 30-45 degrees out
Hinge at hips, bend knees, grip bar with arms inside legs
Flatten back, chest up, create tension by pulling slack from bar
Drive through full foot, extending hips and knees simultaneously
Keep bar close to body, finish with lockout by driving hips through
Lower bar with control maintaining back position, repeat

name: Cable Lateral Raise
description: Cable variation of lateral raise providing constant tension throughout movement for shoulder width.
key_principles: Slight forward lean, lead with elbow, raise to shoulder height, control descent, avoid momentum.
key_technical_checkpoints: Cable from low position, elbow slightly bent, raise to shoulder level, thumb slightly down.
instructions: Stand sideways to cable machine, grab handle with far hand, cable at low position
Step away to create tension, slight bend in elbow, lean slightly away from cable
Raise arm out to side in arc motion until hand reaches shoulder height
Lead with elbow, keep wrist and elbow at same height
Pause briefly at top, lower with control against resistance
Complete all reps, then switch sides

name: Landmine Press
description: Single-arm overhead press using landmine setup, excellent for shoulder strength and core stability.
key_principles: Vertical press path, core engaged, no excessive lean, full extension, controlled eccentric.
key_technical_checkpoints: Landmine secured, elbow under wrist, press to full lockout, maintain square hips and shoulders.
instructions: Load barbell in landmine, face the landmine, feet shoulder-width
Pick up end of barbell at shoulder height, elbow under wrist
Brace core, press barbell up and slightly back to full extension
Keep wrist neutral, drive through full range of motion
Lower with control back to shoulder position
Complete all reps on one side before switching

name: Seated Dumbbell Press
description: Seated overhead press with dumbbells for shoulder development with back support for stability.
key_principles: Back supported, press straight up, full range, control descent, avoid excessive arch.
key_technical_checkpoints: Bench at 85-90 degrees, elbows below wrists, press to lockout overhead, smooth motion.
instructions: Set bench to near-vertical position, sit with back firmly against pad
Bring dumbbells to shoulder height, palms forward, elbows bent
Brace core, press dumbbells straight up until arms fully extended
Avoid hitting dumbbells together at top, keep tension on shoulders
Lower dumbbells with control to shoulder height
Repeat maintaining strict form and full range of motion

name: Bradford Press
description: Continuous press variation moving bar from front to back of head, maintaining constant shoulder tension.
key_principles: Partial range, front to back, constant tension, light weight, strict form, no momentum.
key_technical_checkpoints: Bar stays above head level, controlled transitions, shoulder-width grip, maintain upright posture.
instructions: Load bar with light weight, position in front rack on shoulders
Press bar partially up (not full lockout) to forehead level
Move bar behind head to back of neck without lowering below ear level
Press partially back up, return bar to front position
Continue alternating front to back, maintaining tension throughout
Complete desired reps or time, constant motion without rest

name: Cable Tricep Overhead Extension
description: Overhead cable extension targeting tricep long head with arms overhead position for maximum stretch.
key_principles: Elbows high and forward, only forearms move, full stretch, controlled extension, squeeze at bottom.
key_technical_checkpoints: Face away from cable, rope behind head, elbows stationary, full extension, slow eccentric.
instructions: Set cable at low position, attach rope handle, face away from machine
Grip rope overhead with both hands, step forward to create tension
Position elbows high beside head, rope behind head at starting position
Extend arms overhead by contracting triceps until arms straight
Squeeze triceps at full extension for a moment
Lower with control feeling stretch in triceps, repeat

name: Concentration Curl
description: Isolated bicep curl with elbow braced against inner thigh for strict form and peak contraction.
key_principles: Elbow stationary, full supination, squeeze at top, slow eccentric, no momentum.
key_technical_checkpoints: Seated position, elbow inside thigh, full range, wrist supinated at top, controlled throughout.
instructions: Sit on bench, spread legs, hold dumbbell in one hand
Brace elbow against inside of same-side thigh, arm extended
Curl dumbbell up toward shoulder keeping elbow stationary
Rotate wrist to full supination at top, squeeze bicep hard
Lower with control to full arm extension without losing tension
Complete all reps before switching arms

name: EZ Bar Curl
description: Bicep curl using EZ bar for reduced wrist strain and effective bicep development.
key_principles: Elbows at sides, controlled curl, full range, no swinging, constant tension.
key_technical_checkpoints: Grip on angled portion, elbows fixed, curl to full contraction, slow descent.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width, grip EZ bar at angled portions
Let arms hang fully extended, elbows close to sides
Curl bar up toward shoulders by contracting biceps
Keep elbows stationary throughout movement, no swinging
Squeeze biceps at top for peak contraction
Lower bar with control to full extension, repeat

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
description: Overhead dumbbell extension for triceps emphasizing long head with deep stretch.
key_principles: Elbows close to head, deep stretch, controlled movement, squeeze at top, bilateral or unilateral.
key_technical_checkpoints: Dumbbell behind head, elbows pointing up, full extension, no elbow flare.
instructions: Stand or sit with dumbbell held with both hands overhead
Keep upper arms vertical with elbows pointing up and close to head
Lower dumbbell behind head by bending elbows until deep stretch felt
Keep elbows as stationary as possible throughout movement
Extend arms by contracting triceps until arms straight overhead
Squeeze triceps briefly at top, lower with control, repeat

name: Zottman Curl
description: Curl variation combining supinated curl up and pronated lower for complete arm development.
key_principles: Supinate on way up, pronate at top, control eccentric, full range, targets biceps and forearms.
key_technical_checkpoints: Palms up during curl, rotate at top, palms down during lowering, elbows stationary.
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at sides, arms extended, palms forward
Curl dumbbells up toward shoulders with standard supinated curl
At top of movement, rotate wrists so palms face down (pronated)
Lower dumbbells slowly in pronated position back to start
At bottom, rotate wrists back to palms-up position
Immediately begin next rep, continuous motion

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: Intense core exercise using ab wheel, training anti-extension strength and full core stability.
key_principles: Brace core hard, controlled rollout, prevent lower back arch, use hips to return, progressive range.
key_technical_checkpoints: Neutral spine maintained, full extension if able, no hip sag, controlled throughout.
instructions: Kneel on pad with ab wheel in front, hands on handles
Brace core maximally, engage glutes to prevent back arch
Slowly roll wheel forward extending arms and body
Maintain rigid core, go as far as possible while keeping back neutral
Squeeze core and glutes to roll back to starting position
Start with shorter range, progress to full extension over time

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: Fundamental gymnastic position building total core strength and body tension awareness.
key_principles: Lower back pressed to floor, legs and shoulders off ground, constant tension, breathe steadily.
key_technical_checkpoints: No lower back arch, chin tucked, arms extended overhead, legs straight, controlled breathing.
instructions: Lie on back, press lower back into floor by engaging abs
Extend arms overhead, legs straight, point toes
Raise shoulders and legs off floor 6-12 inches
Press lower back down continuously, creating 'hollow' body position
Hold this position breathing steadily, no arching allowed
Start with 10-20 seconds, progress to longer holds

name: Cable Crunch
description: Kneeling cable crunch allowing progressive overload for abdominal development.
key_principles: Rope to forehead, crunch down, squeeze abs, controlled return, weight progression possible.
key_technical_checkpoints: Rope behind head, knees on pad, hip flexion minimal, spine flexion emphasized.
instructions: Kneel facing high cable with rope attachment, pull rope to forehead
Hold rope behind or beside head, elbows in fixed position
Crunch downward by flexing spine, bringing elbows toward knees
Focus on abs doing the work, minimize hip flexion
Squeeze abs hard at bottom position, hold briefly
Return to start with control maintaining tension, repeat

name: Dragon Flag
description: Bruce Lee's famous exercise requiring extreme core strength and control of entire body.
key_principles: Body rigid as a board, lower with control, minimal lower back contact, shoulder blade pivot point.
key_technical_checkpoints: Grip bench behind head, body straight, lower to near-parallel, raise without momentum.
instructions: Lie on bench, grip edges behind head firmly for stability
Raise entire body except shoulder blades off bench, body straight
Keep body rigid, slowly lower legs and torso toward horizontal
Maintain straight body line, control descent with core strength
Before touching bench, use abs to raise body back to vertical
Start with partial range, progress gradually over weeks/months

name: Pallof Press
description: Anti-rotation exercise training core stability by resisting rotational forces from cable.
key_principles: Square hips and shoulders, press out and resist rotation, core engaged throughout, controlled tempo.
key_technical_checkpoints: Cable at chest height, perpendicular stance, full extension without rotation, slow return.
instructions: Set cable at chest height, stand perpendicular to machine
Hold handle with both hands at chest, step away for tension
Stand with feet shoulder-width, brace core to resist rotation
Press handle straight out from chest, resist cable's pull to rotate
Hold extended position briefly maintaining square hips and shoulders
Return handle to chest with control, repeat all reps, then switch sides

name: Battle Ropes
description: High-intensity rope exercise building cardiovascular endurance, grip strength, and power.
key_principles: Athletic stance, generate power from hips, maintain rhythm, work intervals, breathe steadily.
key_technical_checkpoints: Slight knee bend, core engaged, arms alternate or simultaneous, rope waves consistent.
instructions: Face anchor point with rope ends in each hand, feet shoulder-width
Bend knees slightly, hinge at hips, engage core for athletic stance
Create waves by alternating arms up and down with power
Generate force from core and hips, not just arms
Maintain consistent wave amplitude and tempo throughout interval
Work for 20-30 seconds, rest, repeat for multiple rounds

name: Prowler Push
description: Weighted sled push for building lower body power, strength endurance, and conditioning.
key_principles: Low body position, drive through legs, maintain pace, push through full foot, progressive loading.
key_technical_checkpoints: Arms extended, torso angled forward, legs drive powerfully, short powerful steps.
instructions: Load prowler/sled with appropriate weight, grip high or low handles
Position body leaning into sled, arms extended, athletic stance
Drive through legs taking short, powerful steps
Keep core braced, maintain forward lean throughout
Push for distance (15-40 meters) at consistent pace
Rest as needed, repeat for multiple rounds or distances

name: Broad Jump
description: Explosive horizontal jump testing and building lower body power and athletic performance.
key_principles: Swing arms, load hips, explode forward, land softly, full body coordination.
key_technical_checkpoints: Hip hinge load, arm swing for momentum, jump for distance, soft landing, balance on landing.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width, prepare for broad jump
Swing arms back while hinging at hips, loading legs like a spring
Explode forward swinging arms forward for momentum
Drive through legs, extend hips forcefully, jump for maximum distance
Land on both feet simultaneously, absorbing impact with bent knees
Stick landing with balance, reset, repeat for desired reps

name: Tuck Jump
description: Maximum vertical jump bringing knees to chest, developing explosive power and reactivity.
key_principles: Maximum effort, quick ground contact, bring knees high, land softly, minimize ground time between reps.
key_technical_checkpoints: Arms help drive up, knees to chest at peak, soft landing, immediate rebound if doing continuous.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width in athletic ready position
Dip down quickly into quarter squat, arms swing back
Explode upward jumping as high as possible, swing arms up
Pull knees up toward chest at peak height of jump
Extend legs before landing, land softly on balls of feet
If doing multiple reps, quickly rebound into next jump

name: Assault Bike Sprint
description: High-intensity air bike sprints using arms and legs simultaneously for metabolic conditioning.
key_principles: Full body effort, push and pull arms, drive with legs, maintain high cadence, interval-based.
key_technical_checkpoints: Proper seat height, both arms and legs working, maintain pace, controlled breathing.
instructions: Set seat height so slight knee bend at bottom of pedal stroke
Grip handles firmly, feet secured in pedal straps
Begin sprinting using both arms and legs at maximum effort
Push and pull handles while driving legs through full pedal stroke
Maintain highest sustainable cadence for sprint duration (20-60 seconds)
Rest for 1-2 minutes or recovery interval, repeat for desired rounds

name: Neck Flexion
description: Forward neck strengthening exercise building anterior neck muscles and improving posture.
key_principles: Controlled movement, gentle resistance, never jerk, progressive overload, maintain alignment.
key_technical_checkpoints: Smooth motion, no jerking, controlled resistance, neutral spine, breathe steadily.
instructions: Lie on back on bench with head hanging off edge
Place light weight plate or towel on forehead for resistance
Slowly tuck chin and lift head up toward chest
Hold briefly at top position with controlled tension
Lower head back down with control to starting position
Repeat for desired reps, never use momentum or jerking

name: Neck Extension
description: Backward neck strengthening targeting posterior neck muscles for balanced development.
key_principles: Gentle resistance, controlled tempo, no excessive range, build gradually, proper breathing.
key_technical_checkpoints: Face down position, smooth extension, no hyperextension, equal tempo up and down.
instructions: Lie face down on bench with head hanging off edge
Place light weight plate or hands on back of head for resistance
Slowly extend neck raising head up toward ceiling
Keep movement controlled, don't hyperextend neck
Hold briefly at top with posterior neck muscles engaged
Lower head back to start position with control, repeat

name: Neck Lateral Flexion
description: Side neck strengthening for lateral flexors, important for complete neck development.
key_principles: Lie sideways, controlled motion, equal both sides, light resistance, no jerking.
key_technical_checkpoints: Sideways position, ear toward shoulder, controlled throughout, same reps both sides.
instructions: Lie on side on bench with head hanging off edge
Place light weight plate or hand on side of head
Slowly lift head sideways bringing ear toward shoulder
Keep movement in frontal plane, no rotation
Hold briefly at top position, lower with control
Complete all reps on one side, then switch to other side

name: Neck Isometric Holds
description: Static neck strengthening using isometric holds in multiple directions for stability.
key_principles: No movement, push into resistance, hold steady tension, all directions, breathing continues.
key_technical_checkpoints: Position held, consistent pressure, no movement, balanced effort all directions.
instructions: Sit or stand with good posture, place hand on forehead
Push head forward into hand while resisting with hand
Hold this isometric contraction for 10-20 seconds
Repeat with hand on back of head pushing backward
Repeat with hand on each side of head
Maintain steady breathing, never hold breath during holds

name: Neck Rotations (Controlled)
description: Controlled neck rotations for mobility, warm-up, and maintaining healthy range of motion.
key_principles: Slow and controlled, full range safely, no forcing, both directions equally, relaxed shoulders.
key_technical_checkpoints: Smooth motion, no jerking, comfortable range, shoulders down, even tempo.
instructions: Sit or stand with shoulders relaxed and down
Slowly turn head to look over one shoulder as far as comfortable
Hold briefly, feeling gentle stretch
Return to center with control
Rotate to opposite side, same range and tempo
Continue alternating sides for desired reps or time

name: Bicycle Crunch (Obliques)
description: Dynamic core exercise emphasizing obliques through rotation and opposite elbow-to-knee movement.
key_principles: Rotate through core, opposite elbow to knee, controlled tempo, full extension, breathe rhythmically.
key_technical_checkpoints: Lower back pressed down, rotate from core, full leg extension, steady pace.
instructions: Lie on back, hands behind head, legs extended, lower back pressed to floor
Bring one knee toward chest while lifting shoulder and rotating torso
Touch opposite elbow to knee at peak of crunch
Simultaneously extend other leg straight out hovering above ground
Switch sides in fluid pedaling motion, rotating through core
Continue alternating with controlled rhythm for desired reps

name: Wood Chop
description: Diagonal cable chop movement training rotational power and oblique strength.
key_principles: Rotate through core, diagonal path, hips and shoulders move together, control the weight.
key_technical_checkpoints: Cable high to low, pivot on back foot, arms stay extended, full core rotation.
instructions: Set cable at high position, stand sideways to machine, grab handle with both hands
Start with arms extended up near cable, rotate torso toward cable
Pull cable down and across body in diagonal chopping motion
Rotate through hips and core, pivot on back foot
Finish with hands outside opposite hip, core fully rotated
Return with control, complete all reps one side, then switch

name: Reverse Wood Chop
description: Low-to-high diagonal cable movement targeting obliques and rotational strength.
key_principles: Rotate from hips, low to high path, controlled movement, maintain tension, core driven.
key_technical_checkpoints: Cable low to high, pivot feet, arms extended, full rotation, explosive but controlled.
instructions: Set cable at low position, stand sideways, grip handle with both hands
Start in athletic stance with hands at low position near cable
Rotate and lift cable up and across body in diagonal path
Pivot on feet, extend through hips, rotate core powerfully
Finish with arms extended high on opposite side
Control back to start, complete all reps, then switch sides

name: Side Bend (Dumbbell)
description: Standing dumbbell side bend isolating obliques through lateral flexion.
key_principles: Pure lateral movement, controlled bend, stretch opposite side, no forward/back lean, light weight.
key_technical_checkpoints: Stand tall, bend directly to side, dumbbell slides down leg, opposite oblique stretches.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width, hold dumbbell in one hand at side
Place other hand behind head or on hip for balance
Keep shoulders back, bend directly to weighted side
Let dumbbell slide down leg, feeling stretch on opposite side
Contract obliques to return to upright position
Complete all reps on one side before switching to other side

name: Hanging Oblique Raise
description: Advanced hanging exercise bringing knees to side targeting obliques with rotation.
key_principles: Hang dead, rotate hips, bring knees to side, controlled lower, no swinging.
key_technical_checkpoints: Dead hang start, knees come to side not center, hip rotation, slow eccentric.
instructions: Hang from pull-up bar with overhand grip, arms fully extended
Engage core, rotate hips and bring knees up toward one elbow
Focus on oblique contraction pulling knees to the side
Hold briefly at top with knees elevated and rotated
Lower legs with control back to dead hang
Alternate sides each rep or complete all reps one side first

name: Landmine Rotation
description: Rotational power exercise using landmine for explosive oblique and core strength.
key_principles: Explosive rotation, pivot on feet, arms stay extended, drive from hips and core.
key_technical_checkpoints: Landmine setup, hold bar at chest, rotate side to side, feet pivot, power from core.
instructions: Load barbell in landmine, grip end with both hands at chest level
Stand with feet shoulder-width, arms extended holding bar at chest
Explosively rotate torso to one side, pivoting on feet
Keep arms relatively straight, power comes from core and hips
Rotate to opposite side in fluid motion, like swinging bat
Continue alternating sides with power and control

name: Glute Bridge
description: Fundamental hip extension exercise activating glutes and building hip strength.
key_principles: Drive through heels, squeeze glutes at top, maintain neutral spine, full hip extension.
key_technical_checkpoints: Feet flat, knees bent 90 degrees, shoulders on ground, hips fully extended, glutes squeezed.
instructions: Lie on back with knees bent, feet flat on floor hip-width apart
Arms at sides or across chest, shoulders pressed into floor
Drive through heels, lift hips up toward ceiling
Squeeze glutes hard at top, creating straight line from knees to shoulders
Hold briefly maintaining glute contraction
Lower hips with control, lightly touch ground, repeat

name: Frog Pump
description: High-rep glute activation exercise with feet together, excellent for glute pump and mind-muscle connection.
key_principles: Feet together, knees out, squeeze glutes, high reps, constant tension, controlled tempo.
key_technical_checkpoints: Soles of feet together, knees wide, hips fully extended, glutes contract maximally.
instructions: Lie on back, bring soles of feet together letting knees fall out to sides
Position feet relatively close to glutes, frog-leg position
Drive through outside edges of feet, thrust hips up
Squeeze glutes as hard as possible at top position
Lower hips partway down maintaining tension, don't rest on ground
